headlines.title: Oakland police investigate early-morning shooting on Rilea Way
headlines.description: The Oakland Police Department is investigating an early-morning shooting that left a victim hospitalized Sunday. Officers responded to a report of a shooting just after 2:30 a.m. in the 4300 block of Rilea Way. Upon arrival, officers located a victim suffering from an apparent gunshot wound, according to the Oakland Police Department. The victim was transported to a hospital and was last reported in stable condition. According to a preliminary investigation, the suspect allegedly assaulted the victim and pointed a firearm at them. As the victim raised an arm to defend themselves, they were shot. The suspect then allegedly pistol-whipped the victim before fleeing on foot. The identities of the parties involved were not immediately available. The investigation is ongoing. Authorities ask anyone with information to contact the Felony Assault Unit at 510-238-3426 or via email at cidvideos@oaklandca.gov.

headlines.title: Multi-agency drug bust dismantles large-scale meth lab in Central Valley desert
headlines.description: Federal and local law enforcement agencies have successfully dismantled a large-scale clandestine methamphetamine conversion lab housed inside a residence in a rural desert neighborhood in the Central Valley, the Drug Enforcement Administration’s San Francisco Division announced Monday. The operation was led by DEA San Francisco agents in coordination with the Kern County Sheriff’s Office and the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department following an intensive narcotics investigation. Due to the extreme hazards posed by large quantities of hazardous, unknown chemicals inside the residence, on-site lab personnel were assisted by the San Bernardino County Fire Department’s Hazmat unit to safely process the dangerous and unsanitary facility. The bust yielded major seizures and arrests, including: — Five suspects arrested from Sinaloa, Mexico. — 574 pounds of methamphetamine seized. — 1,567 pounds of methamphetamine in solution seized. — Three firearms seized. — Several thousand dollars in U.S. currency seized.

headlines.title: Oakland's Children's Fairyland receives $5M state investment for historic park upgrades
headlines.description: Children’s Fairyland in Oakland is receiving a $5 million state investment to ensure the nearly 80-year-old storybook park can preserve its magic for generations to come. For generations of Bay Area families, Children’s Fairyland has been a place where fairy tales, play, and imagination come to life. The funding comes directly from the state budget and completes the first phase of the park’s long-term capital plan. “This is such an iconic piece of Oakland,” said Kymberly Miller, CEO of Children’s Fairyland. “It is a huge part of what being an Oaklander is and an East Bay icon, so this is real for us. It is giving us what we need to make the future.” Of the total funding, $2 million will support operations, while another $3 million will fund restoration and upgrades, including replacing 100-year-old pipes. “A foundational beginning,” Miller said. “We have a long way to go, we have to improve the physical space of the park, which means maintenance of sets, maybe some new buildings so we can have indoor programming during the winter.” Fairyland celebrated 75 years in Oakland last year. Its storybook world made it a pioneer in children’s entertainment, though the park has also weathered major challenges, including the pandemic. Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee emphasized that the investment ensures families will continue having a place to play and make memories. “It’s vital funding that we need right here in Oakland,” Mayor Lee said, adding, “It’s really a storybook that comes to life. And so regardless of how old you are or how young you are, my family can attest to the fact. This is a dream come true.” In a statement, Assemblymember Mia Bonta said she is proud to deliver real funding wins that preserve the artistic and cultural legacy of Oakland. Miller noted that the support represents a broader endorsement of the park’s mission: “I think our local leaders and Governor Newsom have given Fairyland a vote of confidence. The time is now to come close to Fairyland, get involved whether it is volunteering your time or energy or your treasure to make sure we last the next 76 years.”

headlines.title: Santa Clara County kicks off early voting, mail-in ballots amid heightened security focus
headlines.description: Early voting officially got underway in Santa Clara County as election officials began mailing out more than 1 million ballots to voters ahead of the Nov. 3 election. The Santa Clara County Registrar of Voters also marked the milestone by hosting a media day in conjunction with the county sheriff to address election security and integrity. The proactive messaging comes in response to repeated, unproven claims by President Trump accusing California of “rigging” elections. At the registrar’s office on Berger Drive in San Jose, in-person voting is now open, complemented by about 100 drop boxes set up throughout the county. While some voters remain unfazed by the rhetoric, others noted that the national conversation influenced how they chose to cast their ballots. “I have complete trust in the election system,” said San Jose voter May Lee. “I don’t have any concerns about in-person versus mail-in voting. I personally always go in-person because I feel like I want to ‘engage’ actively in the process and go on the day to vote.” Another San Jose voter, Marina Moreno, said political controversy motivated her to vote in person rather than risking mail-in options. “Right now because of what Trump is going through… saying that he can push votes and stuff like that, I don’t want that to happen to my vote,” Moreno said. When asked if she feared presidential interference rather than a rigged election, she replied, “Yes.” To combat potential disruptions and reassure the public, the registrar has coordinated closely with law enforcement. County officials outlined various safety measures, including low-key patrols by sheriff’s deputies at voting locations. “It could be protesters, electioneering, anything like that, so we do work closely to have a variety of contingency plans in place,” said Matt Moreles of the Registrar of Voters. “We are doing everything we can here at the County to ensure that everybody has a safe and secure experience at the voting locations and that voters can cast their ballots free from any intimidation or interference.” California Attorney General Rob Bonta echoed those commitments, noting that the state is prepared to deploy election observers if needed, just as it did during previous elections when federal monitors were present, to ensure voters feel safe and laws are followed. Registrar voting booths in San Jose on Berger Drive are open during normal business hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with additional in-person voting centers slated to open across the county on Oct. 24.

headlines.title: Bankruptcy judge rejects Oakland Diocese plan to resolve hundreds of sex abuse claims
headlines.description: A federal bankruptcy judge has rejected a plan from the Diocese of Oakland that would resolve nearly 350 sexual abuse claims and chart a path out of Chapter 11. Plaintiffs’ attorneys celebrated the decision after nearly every survivor with a pending claim opposed the plan. “Now, hopefully, we can work with the bishop to bring speedy justice to the suffering,” said attorney Jeff Anderson, who represents survivors with claims against the Diocese. “For over three years, the Bishop and his lawyer, bankruptcy lawyers, have deployed hardball tactics to further oppress and suppress justice, truth, and transparency that the survivors seek through the creditors committee.” In his 109-page ruling, U.S. Bankruptcy Judge William Lafferty detailed his issues with the plan and found the Diocese failed to satisfy a key test in bankruptcy court: That dissenting creditors “receive at least as much in the proposed plan” as they would in a liquidation. The judge ruled the diocese should not be treated differently in court simply because it’s a religious entity. He also took issue with how it valued its assets. Lafferty encouraged “continuing dialogue and relentless good faith” as both sides resumed working towards a resolution. In a message to Catholics within the Oakland Diocese, Bishop Michael Barber said Judge Lafferty laid out what needs to be corrected with the plan and that the Diocese will study the court’s decision. “While this is a setback, we remain committed to providing fair and equitable treatment for the survivors, and to continuing our mission to proclaim the Gospel of Jesus Christ in service to the 500,000 faithful Catholics in our community,” Barber said.

headlines.title: Couple found dead at Oakland Hills home identified as owners of fashion company
headlines.description: A couple found shot to death outside their Oakland Hills home last week has been identified as Michelle Min and Bryan Walker, police officials announced Monday. The founders of fashion brand Bryn Walker, Min, 63, and Walker, 64, were found outside their home in the 400 block of Panoramic Way, close to the Berkeley border, after a neighbor reported hearing gunshots Friday at about 10:45 a.m. The address is within the Panoramic Hills neighborhood along the border with Berkeley, near the campus of the University of California. Oakland Assistant Police Chief Casey Johnson said at the time that the pair, who appeared to be married, were discovered outdoors after officers responded to a call from a neighbor. A firearm was located at the scene, according to Johnson, who said police had not confirmed if the case was a double murder or murder-suicide. There was no threat to the neighborhood and police weren’t looking for other suspects, Johnson said. The couple owned and operated Bryn Walker, a Berkeley-based fashion design company with retail shops and a wholesale operation that was founded in 1991, according to state businesses license records. Anyone with information about the case can call the Oakland Police Department at 510-238-3821 or the tip line at 510-238-7950. Video and photos can be sent to cidvideos@oaklandca.gov.

headlines.title: Morgan Hill man arrested after allegedly killing wife and driving body to San Jose hospital
headlines.description: A Morgan Hill man is in custody following a disturbing murder investigation after police say he killed his wife and drove her body to a San Jose hospital. Roy Anthony Lopez, 37, was taken into custody Saturday after arriving at Good Samaritan Hospital in San Jose with his wife in the passenger seat. Morgan Hill police noted that a recent mugshot of Lopez was not available, releasing a previous booking photo from an unrelated arrest instead. Police say Lopez told hospital staff that he had killed his wife. Paramedics attempted life-saving measures, but she was pronounced dead inside a car in the hospital parking lot. San Jose police detained Lopez and notified the Morgan Hill Police Department, determining the homicide occurred at a home near Vintage Lane in Morgan Hill. Investigators reported finding evidence of a homicide inside the residence. “During the investigation officers determined that it had been committed in Morgan Hill and that the subject then drove the victim to Good Samaritan,” said Sgt. Sean Bayard of the Morgan Hill Police Department. The discovery sparked immediate concern for the couple’s three children—ages 14, 6, and 3—who were inside the home at the time and may have witnessed the attack. “They were at the house we believe at the time, and they are in safe custody right now,” Sgt. Bayard said. Neighbors expressed shock at the violence in the otherwise quiet neighborhood, reporting a heavy police presence outside the home for hours Saturday before details of the tragedy emerged. “Police were here for quite a few hours,” said neighbor Pranhleen Bariana. “It’s heartbreaking. No circumstances justify taking a significant other’s life.” Authorities have not yet released the victim’s identity, pending notification of family by the coroner’s office. Investigators noted that a firearm was not used in the killing, though an official cause of death has not been publicly disclosed. As the investigation continues, police are working to piece together the motive, including why Lopez drove to the San Jose hospital. “We want to let them know that we’re doing our best to follow anything we can on this case so we can present this to the DA office to help them in the prosecution of it,” Sgt. Bayard said. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Morgan Hill police Sgt. Bayard by phone at 408-607-3032 or by email at sean.bayard@morganhill.ca.gov. If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline by calling 1-800-799-SAFE (7233), visiting www.thehotline.org or texting LOVEIS to 22522.

headlines.title: Bay Area heat advisory extended through Thursday
headlines.description: Much of the Bay Area is facing hot weather through Thursday, with moderate to major heat risks expected across inland communities, the National Weather Service said Monday. The hottest areas will be inland valleys, where temperatures are expected to reach the mid-80s to low 100s. The forecast calls for highs around 100 degrees in Concord and Livermore, 96 in Napa and Santa Rosa, and 93 in San Jose on Monday. A heat advisory remains in effect through 10 p.m. Thursday for much of the interior Bay Area and Central Coast. The weather service warned that the heat can affect people without adequate cooling or hydration and advised residents to move outdoor activities to cooler parts of the day and never leave people or pets unattended in vehicles. The heat will also raise fire danger in higher terrain through Thursday. Major HeatRisk is expected to remain widespread in parts of the East Bay through Tuesday and across the Santa Clara Valley through Wednesday. Meanwhile, coastal flooding and beach hazards are expected to become a concern beginning Wednesday as high tides push water farther inland along some coastal and bayshore areas. The risks are expected to continue through Sunday. Coastal flooding could affect low-lying roads, parks and trails, while beachgoers should watch for rip currents and sneaker waves. headlines.title: Race for CA insurance commissioner: Once-boring contest is now high stakes
headlines.description: California voters will choose between two Democrats with differing visions for the state’s troubled insurance market when they elect a new insurance commissioner this November. Jane Kim, a former San Francisco supervisor, and Ben Allen, a state senator representing the West Los Angeles region, advanced to the run-off after neither candidate won a majority of the votes in the June primary election. A recent poll showed Kim has nearly 25% of respondents supported Kim while 18% supported Allen. Despite the appearance of Kim’s solid lead, more than 57% of the 1,000 people surveyed said they are undecided. Kim and Allen both seem to agree a major overhaul is needed in California’s insurance system, especially after California has experienced devastating disasters, including wildfires and flooding. But they have a different approach to fixing the current insurance system. One of Kim’s key policy proposals is creating a single-payer disaster insurance system, modeled after programs in New Zealand, Spain and France. While homeowners are free to purchase private policies, the state would provide a guaranteed — automatic and universal — home disaster insurance policy, under Kim’s plan. But critics said Kim’s proposal does not specify how costly and realistic it would be for the state government to operate such a system. Others also worry Kim’s plans would further drive out insurers from California. Allen, whose home was affected in the 2025 Palisades Fire, has a different approach than Kim: the state senator wants to reform the existing insurance system to bring insurers back to California. To make the current model work, Allen wants to “modernize rate-setting,” the process insurers use to calculate premiums based on expected claims, risk factors, operating costs and regulatory requirements. He also wants to make California less vulnerable to future disasters by expanding consumer protections and supporting wildfire-resilient homes and communities. However, Allen’s proposals may make him look like the establishment, not being tough enough on insurers. Critics worry that Allen’s plans would favor insurers over Californians, who have struggled with policy cancelations and high premiums. Elections Sep 30 Kim is endorsed by progressive leaders, such as U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders, labor leader David Huerta and outgoing Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis. Allen’s supporters include U.S. senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla as well as California Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas.

headlines.title: New tool aims to make it even easier to be an informed voter
headlines.description: A new tool aims to make it even faster and more convenient for voters to gather election information. OpenBallot.app, started by a group of tech-savvy Bay Area entrepreneurs, allows voters to find information they need to compare candidates and learn about ballot propositions without the paperwork that comes in the mail. “When you go to OpenBallot, right away, boom, you see all the voter guides right there,” OpenBallot.app co-founder Rose Bloomin said. “You don’t have to log in. You don’t have to do anything.” OpenBallot.app is nonpartisan. California voters can access it on their smartphones or computers. Right now, voters can find election information for statewide offices and propositions, as well as local races in San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose, San Diego and Los Angeles. The group hopes to broaden the site to include other cities and other states in the future.

headlines.title: Hispanic Heritage Month spotlight: La Raza Historical Society
headlines.description: La Raza Historical Society is documenting and archiving the rich history of Silicon Valley. headlines.title: Fatal crash shuts down lanes on northbound I-280 in San Jose
headlines.description: A multiple-vehicle crash early Monday morning killed at least one person and temporarily shut down three northbound lanes on Interstate Highway 280 in San Jose, according to the California Highway Patrol. The crash was first reported at about 5:40 a.m. just north of State Route 87. Around 6:30 a.m., three lanes were closed and traffic was diverted off the freeway. The lanes have since reopened. The CHP did not immediately provide details about the people involved or what caused the crash. Bay City News contributed to this report
